fields.title: What each field controls
fields.intro: Every input above feeds a specific part of the formula. Here's what each one does and why it matters.

tariff.title: Tariff (€/kWh)
tariff.body: The price the customer currently pays for one kilowatt-hour of grid electricity. Used to convert their monthly bill back into kWh of consumption — the starting point of the whole calculation. If this is wrong, every downstream number is wrong.

irradiance.title: Irradiance (kWh/kWp/year)
irradiance.body: How much energy a 1 kWp system actually produces per year in your country, on a south-facing tilted roof. Comes from the EU's PVGIS database. Bigger number = smaller system needed for the same bill.

derating.title: System derating
derating.body: Real-world losses: inverter inefficiency (~3%), panel soiling (~2%), high-temperature de-rating in summer, wiring losses, etc. The 0.80 default means the system delivers 80% of its theoretical output. Higher derating = smaller (cheaper) system.

cost.title: Cost per kWp (€)
cost.body: Turn-key install cost — panels, inverter, mounting, labour, permits — for one kWp of system. €1,000/kWp is the Kosovo residential mid; bumps when global panel prices rise.

variance.title: Cost variance
variance.body: How wide the cost-range bracket is around the mid estimate. 0.10 = ±10%, so a €13,500 mid renders as €12,150–€14,850. Wider = more honest about uncertainty; narrower = looks more confident but risks under-quoting.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer (EN + SQ)
disclaimer.body: Shown directly under the result on the homepage so customers know this is an estimate, not a binding quote. If you change the tariff or irradiance, also update the disclaimer's reference year — keeping math + legalese in sync is why they live in the same row.

roof.title: Roof factor (not editable)
roof.body: The customer picks one of three roof types. Each modifies the irradiance to reflect real-world performance vs. the south-facing-tilted reference.
roof.flat: Flat roof; ballast or low-tilt mounting rarely hits optimal angle, ~5% loss.
roof.unknown: Customer hasn't told us — we err on the side of slightly bigger system.

formula.title: The formula, step by step
formula.intro: Five steps from monthly bill to payback years. Every customer estimate runs exactly this on the server.

monthlyKwh.title: 1. Bill → energy consumed
monthlyKwh.body: Divide the monthly bill by the tariff to get kWh consumed per month, then multiply by 12 for a yearly figure.

requiredKwp.title: 2. How big a system covers that?
requiredKwp.body: Divide the annual consumption by what 1 kWp of solar actually produces in real-world conditions on this roof.

roundQuarter.title: 3. Round up to the nearest 0.25
roundQuarter.body: Real systems come in whole-panel increments. We round up so we never undersize — better to overshoot a hair than leave the customer short.

cost.title: 4. Install cost (with a range)
cost.body: Multiply the system size by your cost-per-kWp to get the mid estimate, then bracket it by the variance for a low/high range.
cost.expr: mid = system_kWp × cost_per_kWp;  range = mid × (1 ± variance)

payback.title: 5. Payback period
payback.body: How many years of saved electricity pay back the install. Uses the mid cost — the customer sees one number, not a range.

example.title: Worked example with your current values
example.intro: Sample customer: €100/month bill, tilted roof, Prishtina. The numbers below recompute as you edit the inputs above — that's how you sanity-check a change before clicking Save.
example.step3: Step 3 — Round up to next 0.25 kWp

explainer.safetyNote: Tip: small changes have big impact. Bumping tariff from 0.08 → 0.10 alone cuts payback from ~11.3 to ~9.0 years for the same bill. Always glance at the live preview before saving.
